solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Driver, say, hit back and forth?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hit from right to left

parts.note: to hit is to flog
and forth asks for hit a second time, now read forwards: to club someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A question about striking something to and fro, with a car driver in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' does double duty in spirit: read 'back' it reverses, read 'forth' it stands as it is. A driver is the longest-hitting stick in a golfer's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a long-hitting wooden-headed example of the sticks used on the links.

clue.text: Clearly evident, spectrum lacking in orange and green

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for orange
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: A colour spectrum missing all but two of its bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectrum lacking in' frames the idea that only two colours are left: orange (O) and green (VERT, the heraldry word).
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, plainly visible rather than hidden.

clue.text: Queen allowed to wear embroidered felt, soft fabric

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so the queen and allowed go inside
embroidered suggests something worked over and altered, so the letters of felt are rearranged

parts.note: Anne was a queen of Great Britain
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A monarch permitted to dress in decorated felt, a soft cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' scrambles felt into FLTE, and 'to wear' has those letters wrapped around the queen and allowed, split after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannelette is a brushed cotton cloth with a napped, cosy texture, used for sheets and nightwear.

clue.text: Cool evangelist, friendly

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
warm means friendly

explanation.surface: A trendy gospel writer who is also affable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts cool and warm side by side as opposites, yet the answer joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means unenthusiastic, so a cool reception is a tepid one.

clue.text: Similar item of furniture introduced to curious father and bride

indicators.note: introduced to means put in among the other letters
curious means odd, so the letters of father and bride are rearranged

parts.note: a sofa is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A settee brought in to meet an inquisitive dad and his daughter on her wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' looks like a description of the father but signals the scramble; 'introduced to' sets the furniture inside the mixed letters, after the fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of a feather are people of like tastes or character, as in the proverb about flocking together.

clue.text: Celebrity currently featuring in musical, not finished

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so one piece goes inside the other
not finished says to drop the final letter

parts.note: Rent is a stage musical
currently means now

explanation.surface: A star now appearing in a stage show that has not yet ended its run.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is a Broadway rock musical; 'not finished' drops its last letter, and 'featuring in' puts the word for currently inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame, the state of being celebrated.

clue.text: Shakespearean character inspiring a film actor later taking bigger role

definitions.text: film actor later taking bigger role

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the character takes the letter inside

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: A role from Shakespeare motivating a screen actor who later moved to a larger part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' is read as breathing in: REGAN takes A inside. The bigger role was the US presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan acted in Hollywood films before becoming US president, a far larger part.

clue.text: Duck in long river, dropping tail

indicators.note: dropping tail means losing the last letter

parts.note: the Nile is the world's longest river

explanation.surface: A duck swimming in a great river loses its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is a batsman's score of zero, so it means nothing at all.

clue.text: Wolf — more experienced packs in country

indicators.note: packs in means stuffs inside, so the country goes within the other word

parts.note: more experienced means wiser
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A wolf, older and wiser, roams with packs across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolf' and 'packs' paint an animal picture, but the wolf here is a man who chases women.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf, in slang, is a man who pursues many women, which is a womaniser.

clue.text: Ship ready to be launched possibly in US port

parts.note: something new, freshly built, might be ready for launching
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: A vessel awaiting launch, perhaps in an American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark in New Jersey has one of the busiest container seaports in America.

clue.text: Light plane that's inclined to transport dignitary

indicators.note: to transport means to carry, so the dignitary is held inside

parts.note: a ramp is an inclined plane
an earl is a nobleman, a dignitary

explanation.surface: A light aircraft, banking, used to fly an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the geometric sense: a sloping surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear lamp is the light at the back of a vehicle.

clue.text: Bowl over, with very hot ball trapping opener in test

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the first letter goes within

parts.note: the sun is a very hot ball of gas

indicators.note: opener in means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: bowling in a Test match with the ball and the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'opener' plays on the opening batsman but just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish them, which is to stun them.

clue.text: Drinking suffered, last of pubs boarded up

indicators.note: boarded means went aboard, so the letter gets inside the phrase

parts.note: was ailing means suffered

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone who suffered from drink while the pubs were closed and shuttered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarded up' suggests closed pubs, but it puts S inside WAS AILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is festive carousing, toasting with spiced ale.

clue.text: Tasty punches to the face?

definitions.meaning: read literally, smacking the lips would be blows to the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Lip-smacking food makes you smack your lips in appreciation, so it is delicious.

clue.text: Composer put line in short song: riff not requiring one

indicators.note: put with in means place one piece within another
in, with put, means the line goes inside
short means missing the final letter

parts.note: a carol is a song

indicators.note: not requiring means leave out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to a composer: add a line to a brief song and lose a guitar riff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CAROL to CARO, and 'put ... in' places L in it to give CARLO; 'not requiring one' takes I out of RIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana.

clue.text: Lengthy item calling to the lower house: planner upset about that

definitions.text: Lengthy item calling to the lower

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the house
upset means knocked over, so the letters of planner are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something long summoning MPs to the Commons, a planner unhappy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lower house' looks like the House of Commons, but a lower is a cow, one that lows; 'upset' gives ALPENRN, and 'about' wraps it round HO.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn used by Alpine herders to call their cattle.

clue.text: Having taken some hemp as smuggler, search me!

indicators.note: taken some means a portion of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler, caught with cannabis, says he has no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'pass' means you don't know the answer, as a quiz contestant would, just like 'search me!'.

clue.text: Many use rum on bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lot of cooks use rum on bananas, as in a flambé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit in a recipe but is slang for mad, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, as many does.

clue.text: See spinners spinning

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tops are toys that spin

explanation.surface: Watch the spinning tops twirl.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, which is to see it.

clue.text: Full of goodness, cook tripe

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the exclamation goes inside

parts.note: to fry is to cook
lumme is an old British exclamation of surprise, like goodness!

explanation.surface: A wholesome cook preparing offal.
explanation.walkthrough: LUMME is a dated British exclamation (from 'Lord love me'), here standing for 'goodness!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flummery is empty flattery or nonsense, which tripe also means.

clue.text: By the sound of it, language perfect

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the answer is said like another word

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: A language that seems flawless when you hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfect a piece of work is to finish it, giving it a final polish.

clue.text: Coarse show embodying extremes of evil

indicators.note: embodying means taking into the body, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to indicate is to show

indicators.note: extremes of means first and last letters

explanation.surface: A vulgar entertainment that contains the worst of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a noun for an entertainment but is the verb, INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate means lacking refinement, crude or rude.

clue.text: All those on stage thrown off

definitions.meaning: the full set of actors in a production
... is the past participle of ..., to throw, as in ... off

explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a play are its cast, and cast also means thrown or discarded.

clue.text: Attack winger

definitions.meaning: to attack with sniping remarks or shots
a wading bird, so it has wings

explanation.definitionFit: Sniping is criticising from cover; the snipe is a long-billed marsh bird.

clue.text: Head for Google: previous search one supposedly forgot quickly

indicators.note: head for means the first letter of the word

parts.note: old means previous, as in an old address
to fish is to search, as in fishing for something

explanation.surface: Using Google to look up a past search one quickly forgot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the popular claim that a goldfish has a three-second memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldfish are popularly, and wrongly, believed to have a memory lasting only seconds.

clue.text: Mark Fox turns up

indicators.note: turns up, in a down entry, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark, a sly fox, arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small mark or spot.

clue.text: Mighty Egyptian, huge deity

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, meaning huge
Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A powerful Egyptian figure, an enormous god.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was a major god of ancient Egypt, ruler of the underworld.

clue.text: Grab succeeded, as you'd expect

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
natch is slang for naturally, as you'd expect

explanation.surface: He seized it and won, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to seize something quickly, just as to grab is.

clue.text: Philosophical novel one ends eg with hint of realism

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thoughtful novel that ends with a touch of realism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the adjective new, signalling the rearrangement; the hint of realism, though it comes last in the clue, leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being philosophical about a setback means accepting it calmly, which is being resigned.
